title: Stray Kids Join BTS in Withholding Music From Grammy Consideration
summary:
Stray Kids are reportedly joining BTS in withholding their music from the Grammy Awards process. Billboard says the group's company did not elaborate on the eight-member group's decision to skip Grammy submissions, but it seems likely that it responds to the Recording Academy's recent addition of a best Asian pop music performance category. Billboard has reached out to representatives for Stray Kids and the Grammys for comment.

In July, BTS announced that its members would not participate in the Grammys, despite a massive year that included the album ARIRANG topping the Billboard 200 for three weeks. The group said it was protesting awards "being divided by region or language."

Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. responded at the time that he was saddened but respected the decision. He said he wanted to clarify that submitting in localized, genre-based categories does not bar artists from the general categories. "The Asian pop category was created to celebrate the depth, diversity and extraordinary growth of pop artistry coming out of Asia," he said. "It's never to divide, but to expand who is recognized by our 15,000 Grammy voters."

The category has been a hot topic for months. In early September, the academy held a virtual call with 80-plus artists, executives and stakeholders from the Asian music community to review the award. On Thursday, Oct. 1, the academy confirmed that it will move forward with it. Mason said the academy heard from people who do not support the category, from people who lacked accurate information about it, and from enthusiastic supporters. "We understand this conclusion will not satisfy everyone, and that never feels good," he added, but he said the academy is confident it is the right conclusion for the music community overall.

Stray Kids have had an incredible run even without Grammy recognition. In the past year the group has topped the Billboard 200 twice, with the November EP DO IT and August's THIS & THAT. The title track from THIS & THAT reached No. 38 on the Billboard Hot 100.
why_it_matters: The story shows how an awards group and artists can disagree about whether special categories celebrate music from different places or separate it from the main categories.
